Presumptuous

prih-ZUMP-choo-us · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Presumptuous is overstepping what is proper or appropriate by assuming too much, especially without being asked.

It was presumptuous of the new employee to assign himself the corner office before anyone had discussed seating.

Worked Example

Rather than wait for an invitation, the presumptuous cousin simply brought three extra guests to the wedding reception and expected seats for all of them.

Presumptuous behavior always involves taking something for granted -- permission, space, credit -- that was never actually offered.

How Presumptuous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

overconfident

overconfident: having excessive confidence in oneself

forward

forward: bold or overly familiar, especially toward someone one barely knows

Antonyms

deferential

deferential: showing respect for someone's authority or wishes

modest

modest: not overstepping or claiming too much

How Strong Is It? — forward → shameless → presumptuous

forward vs. presumptuous

forward vs. presumptuous: Being forward is milder -- it just means being overly bold or familiar, without necessarily assuming a specific privilege the way presumptuous does.

shameless vs. presumptuous

shameless vs. presumptuous: Shameless pushes further than presumptuous, describing behavior that isn't just overstepping but doing so without a trace of embarrassment.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of presumptuous.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — pre-

prefix — pre-: before (Latin prae-)

root — -sum-

root — -sum-: to take (Latin sumere)

suffix — -ptuous (-uous)

suffix — -ptuous (-uous): full of, given to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Presumptuous comes from Latin prae- ('before') plus sumere ('to take') and -uous, 'full of, given to' (spelled -ptuous here, keeping the pt of Latin sumptus) -- to be presumptuous is to be full of 'taking before,' grabbing liberties, permission, or credit that was never actually offered.

Use the root in a new word: consume

Use the root in a new word: consume: Consume uses the same sum- ('to take') root as presumptuous -- to consume something is to 'take it in' completely.
